outputs.without:
1. Provision compatibility database views or triggers on the bookstore database so writes written in the new format automatically project into the shape expected by the old reader.
2. Roll out the new writer to a 10% canary slice while keeping existing writers active and monitoring lock contention on shared inventory tables.
3. Execute an idempotent background backfill script for existing inventory and customer records during off-peak hours, logging any rows that fail legacy constraint validation.
4. Scale the new writer to 100% of write traffic and verify zero schema drift across both old-reader endpoints and new-schema queries before scheduling deprecation of the compatibility layer.

Rollback Trigger: Any mismatch detected in hourly shadow-read comparisons above 0.1% of sampled bookstore SKUs, or database deadlock count exceeds 5 per minute.

Smoke Check: Insert a new hardcover edition using the new writer API, query the legacy storefront catalog endpoint for that SKU, and confirm the title, price, and stock count match.
outputs.with:
1. Apply an expand-only database migration in staging that adds the new bookstore schema alongside existing tables, and run the smallest affected contract test suite covering old-reader queries against new-writer rows.
2. Ship the new writer to production behind a feature flag set to OFF, verify the `/health` endpoint responds 200, and review the deployment diff to confirm no unrelated changes touch existing reader behavior.
3. Turn on the new writer for internal staff traffic first, then canary at 5% while dual-writing legacy fields so un-migrated bookstore readers continue serving inventory and pricing without schema drift.
4. Promote the new writer through 25%, 50%, and 100% stages only when error budget burn stays nominal, keeping the old-reader compatibility shim active until all reader pods roll over.

**Rollback trigger:** Immediately revert the writer flag to OFF if old-reader schema validation failures exceed 0.1% of responses or catalog endpoint error rate exceeds 2x the pre-release baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.

**Smoke check:** Exercise the end-to-end bookstore listing flow after deploy: create a test title with the new writer, query it through a pinned old-reader pod (plus a malformed ISBN request to verify the expected 400 contract), and log the exact HTTP statuses and response bodies.

blind: B is stronger than A because it orders expand-only staging contract tests, dormant feature-flagged deploy, internal/5% canary, and 25%/50%/100% error-budget gating while using a 5-minute immediate flag-off trigger instead of an hourly shadow comparison.
